rules.boundary: rule K1: at step 0 and at the first rollout start at or past each multiple of checkpoint_every a checkpoint is saved; then, in every run whether interrupted or not, everything random (python, numpy, torch, the action space and the vec env) is reseeded with 100,000 x seed + 100 x b (b = that multiple / checkpoint_every; env i resets with that + i), every env is reset, the reward normalisation's running returns are zeroed and the model's last observation and episode starts are set from that reset.  A resume loads the newest intact checkpoint without letting the library reset the envs, continues the step count and the schedule, and does the same boundary before its first rollout
rules.checkpoint: a checkpoint is s2load's four files, the record last; its record holds the run state as it is before that step's check (the task weights in force, the fix, the monitor history, the no-gain count, the checks done, any stop, the flags).  Kept locally: each check's and the newest two (rule K2).  When learn() returns, a final checkpoint is saved if the last step has none
rules.resume: rules K4, K5: a resume is refused, in this order, on no run.json; a stopped run; other settings (every argument given must be the run's; the env configs as built today, but for the named freeze and the task names, must be the run's); other inputs (the envs are built from the run's stored configs, which name the freeze the run started on and its tasks: a used file's sha256 or entry hash, the plant's inputs or the resolved task table that differs; a later freeze of the set is accepted when these are unchanged, and both freezes are recorded); other sources than the last session's unless --allow-source-change, or unless an earlier session given it ran on the same sources (SOURCE_ALLOWANCE_RULE); other library versions than the last session's (s2load.comparable) unless --allow-version-change; a checkpoint whose run_uuid or settings hash is not the run's; a fingerprint that is not reproduced within 1e-5.  A checkpoint that fails its integrity check is skipped with its reason.  No intact checkpoint is no refusal: the job restarts from step 0 in place and is the same run.  The run state is taken from the checkpoint's record: run.json's live fields are rebuilt from it (its list of checkpoints holds the step resumed from, whether or not the session that saved it lived to write so), later entries move to the session's discarded_after_resume (the attempts logged for a check on the checkpoint itself are kept), updates.jsonl is cut back to the resumed step, a check that is due at that step and has no record naming that checkpoint is run, and the rules are applied to the records as the uninterrupted run applies them.  A monitor_<n>.json of the resumed step that cannot be read (a copy that was cut short) is no record (rule M1): it is kept beside and the check is run
rules.updates: updates.jsonl holds one line per PPO update: session, update (the run's count), steps (the env steps the policy was trained on after it), minibatch_steps_run (the optimizer steps PPO really made, counted by a wrapper around the optimizer's step: target_kl stops an update without a message, lesson 16) of minibatch_steps_possible, approx_kl, clip_fraction, explained_variance, value_loss, std_mean (the mean of exp(log_std)), lr, ep_len_mean and ep_rew_mean (over the episodes that ended in the update's rollout; the reward before normalisation; null if none ended) and wall_s (the rollout and the update)
rules.kl_cut: rule O3: if the median share of minibatch steps run over a check interval (the updates after the previous check, up to this one) is under one half, run.json carries flags.kl_cut and the lead is told; it stops nothing
rules.rate: gates/rate.json, per session: first_rollout (the session's first rollout: env steps per wall second, no update in it) and first_three (its first three rollouts, two updates included: S2-8's rate), each with the CPU seconds of the trainer and of the workers, the workers, the vCPUs, the resident memory of the trainer and of each worker, and the machine's load.  The clock starts after the session's first boundary, and what the trainer does at later rollout starts (a checkpoint, a check with its monitor child, a boundary) is left out of the wall seconds
rules.gates: gates false (--no-gates): no G8a short form, no R0L baseline and no check, so no G8b, no fix and no stop rule; for validation runs and tests; it is a setting of the run
rules.fine_tune: rule K8: a fine-tune is a new job directory and run id from a parent's checkpoint and statistics (the same layout), the parent's log_std, its own boundaries and checks, and a constant learning rate r: the parent's schedule value p at the parent's step if every minibatch step of each of 6 updates runs at p from the parent's checkpoint, else the largest of 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5, 3e-6 below p at which they all run; if none does the fine-tune does not run
rules.retry: the lead's ruling of 16 Nov 2026 (the fifth list, 2): after the halt for two attempts at one check that were never closed, the lead has the fault repaired and resumes with a recorded parameter (--retry-check; sessions[].retry_check), which lets that check run once more per resume; the attempt is logged with after_halt
rules.baseline: rule M1: R0L's baseline is made once per run, before its first rollout; run.json baseline holds its record's sha256, its summary and, per episode, the condition, the seed, the outcome and the survival (with the state digest where the record holds one).  A resume reads monitor/r0l.json and refuses one that is not the record run.json names.  If the file is lost, or cannot be read (it is then kept beside as r0l.unreadable.s<k>.json), R0L's episodes are run again and compared with what run.json holds, episode for episode and in the summary: equal, the new record takes the old one's place and the session is named under baseline.remade; not equal, the new record is kept as r0l.differs.s<k>.json, nothing is replaced and the run halts and goes to the lead (the run's checks were read against the lost one)
rules.children: an attempt at a check, or at the baseline, holds its monitor child's pid, that process's start time (clock ticks since boot) and the boot id, written when the child has started.  A resume ends, with SIGKILL, every such child of an earlier session on this host that is still alive under an attempt that was never closed (the trainer was killed alone while its monitor ran), before any check or baseline is run: two monitors never write one record.  The attempt stays what it was, an interruption (rule M1); the session lists what it ended under ended_children.  The trainer waits for its monitor child without a timeout (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026): a timeout would close a hung attempt with an exit code and count it toward the two closed attempts; a hang is ended by whoever watches the run, who kills the job's process group, and the attempt that was never closed is an interruption
rules.filter: rule O4 is measured before any run: a run that is not tiny, and rule O3's probe on any set but the Stage 1 view, is refused when filter.json holds no choice, unless the caller names the filter (config filter_hz); a tiny run then takes the env's own default
rules.source_allowance: the lead's ruling 12 of 17 Nov 2026: an allowance for moved sources holds for the rest of the run for the same sources.  A session given --allow-source-change records the hash of the sources it runs on in run.json sources_allowed (with its index), once per hash; a later session whose sources hash is one of them is allowed as if it had been given the parameter: its resume accepts those sources against the last session's (flagged, as with the parameter) and its monitor children get STAGE2_ALLOW_SOURCE_CHANGE=1 for the policy row (rule K9); the session's source_allowance names the session whose parameter allowed them.  Sources that no session given the parameter ran on are allowed only by the parameter.  A halt for moved sources (the monitor's own sources check, or the row's refusal by rule K9) names --allow-source-change, the parameter that resolves it
rules.expect_baseline: rule M3 (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026): with --expect-baseline PATH, the committed R0L baseline (S2-4: stage2/tb/runs/s2-4/R0L_BASELINE.json, made by the monitor's baseline command without a job), the run's own monitor/r0l.json must equal it episode for episode: the condition, the seed, the outcome, the survival and the state digest (monitor2.baseline_equal), with the digests compared in both in every episode that ran (the lead's ruling 33 of 17 Nov 2026: in every pair of which at least one episode ran, both hold a digest that is a non-empty string; two episodes not run, which hold none, are compared on their outcome and survival; with no episode that ran no digest was compared); it is checked after the baseline is made or read and before the first rollout, at every session, and recorded in run.json baseline_expected.  Not equal: the run halts (exit code 5) and goes to the lead; no step is trained.  A file that is missing, cannot be read or is no baseline record, or one given to a run without the gates, is refused before anything is written.  The file's sha256 is a setting of the run (settings.expect_baseline): a resume must give the same file (rule K4)

monitor.episodes: rule M1: 18 episodes: the bar's conditions walk/nominal, walk/v0.4, turn/q90_left, stop/two_step, nudge/forward, nudge/left of the run's set at mu 0.9, three each, condition i (0-5), repetition r (0-2) on seed 6001 + 3 i + r, at 10 ms, as the bar builds and judges them; once per run the same under R0L@10ms.  A tiny run takes each condition's first seed; on the Stage 1 view (set S1, development) the conditions are the stock walk/nominal and walk/brisk
monitor.outcomes: rule M1: each episode ends read, fell, unread (a policy row's episode that did not fall and that the bar could not read: not succeeding in any reading; reason clock_behind when its mean clock factor is below 1, else unreadable) or error (an infrastructure fault).  A policy row's episode is never run twice: an error there counts as not succeeding, as zero credited survival and as not up.  A condition without a reference is not_run: not succeeding and zero survival for both rows.  R0L's episodes must each end read or fell: a baseline that holds an error is kept beside as a failed attempt and no check is read against it
monitor.survival: rule M3: an episode's credited survival is its survival time (the fall time, or the episode's length) times min(1, reference time covered / (1.05 x survival time)): the survival time itself for a row that does not slow its clock.  A clock that covered at least 1.05 x the survival time, to within 1e-9 of it (float rounding), is credited the survival time itself, so that R0L's S is exactly its plain mean survival (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026).  S is the mean over the episodes; N the number succeeding with the look (reading 1).  Printed beside: the counts in readings 2 and 3, the count succeeding but for A1 with the look bands kept, and the plain mean survival, which decide nothing.  The credit needs the episode's clock times (clock.t_ref_reached, clock.t_ref_planned) and its planned length: a policy row's episode that ended read, fell or unread and came back without them is not credited its survival time (a slowed clock would buy it); its table is no record of the check.  R0L, which has no clock to slow, is then credited its survival time
monitor.gain: rule M3: a check shows a gain when N >= N* + 2 or S >= S* + 1.0 s; N* is the largest N, and S* the largest S, over R0L's episodes and every earlier check of the run, each taken separately (for the first check: R0L's)
monitor.m3b: rule M3b (S2-4's reading alone): when the mean planned length of the episodes less R0L's S is under 1.0 s, a gain is also at least 2 more episodes than R0L succeeding in reading 3 with the look bands kept
monitor.g8b: rule M4: at the check of the multiple 5,000,000: walk/nominal stays up (read or unread: it did not fall and is no error) in at least 2 of its 3 episodes.  Otherwise, once: each training task that the table gives to at least one monitor condition with fewer than 2 of 3 up has its weight doubled, once (walk/nominal: walk_nominal; walk/v0.4, nudge/forward, nudge/left: walk_v0.4; turn/q90_left: turn_q90_left and turn_q90_right; stop/two_step: stop and start_stop); the reward's weights do not change.  At the check of the multiple 10,000,000 the same reading; a second failure stops the run.  Checks are named by their multiple.  A tiny run reads at its first check and at the next; with fewer than 3 episodes of a condition "2 of 3" is ceil(2 n / 3) of n
monitor.stop: rule M5: counting from the check of the multiple 20,000,000, the run stops at the third consecutive check without a gain
monitor.attempts: rule M1 with the lead's rulings of 16 Nov 2026: an attempt at a check is logged in run.json monitor[] before the monitor starts, with the checkpoint's file hashes, and closed with the monitor's exit code when it ends.  A record is a monitor_<n>.json that names the checkpoint's hashes and holds an outcome for every one of its episodes.  After two closed attempts that left no record the check counts as without a gain and as a failed G8b reading, each of its episodes an error.  An attempt that was never closed (the session died while the check ran) is an interruption: the resume runs the check again and it does not count; after two of them at one check the run halts and goes to the lead.  A condition without a reference is held in a record as "not run" (the lead's fifth list of 16 Nov 2026, 1).  A monitor that refuses to run is no attempt and is not one of the two (refusal)
monitor.refusal: rule M1 with the lead's ruling of 16 Nov 2026, 19:01 UTC (the fifth list, 6) and the sixth list of 16 Nov 2026 (3): a monitor that refuses to run is no attempt.  It refuses, before any episode, when its sources are not the ones the trainer hashed (the checkout moved under the run), when the run's run.json is missing, cannot be read or is no JSON object, when the checkpoint is not intact (no record, a record that cannot be read or has the wrong shape: its files, and a layout and a fingerprint object, the rulings of 17 Nov 2026, 12; or a file that is not the one its record names), when the checkpoint is another run's (its run_uuid or settings hash is not the run's), when the row refuses the checkpoint while it is built (s2rows.RowError; s2load.CheckpointError: among them a fingerprint not reproduced at the row's load), and when the set is a look set, or a version of one, whose G9-ref has not passed for the body on its latest freeze (rule X1: lookbar.LookSetRefused, raised before the set is read; the lead's ruling 31 of 17 Nov 2026, 6).  The monitor then leaves with exit code 8 and writes its reason to monitor_<n>.refused.json (the baseline: r0l.refused.json).  The trainer closes the attempt with that exit code, marks it refused with the reason, does not count it toward the two closed attempts after which a check counts as without a gain, and halts with exit code 5: the run goes to the lead, and a resume runs the check again (a resume with --retry-check when the refused attempt was the one that parameter let run; a halt for moved sources, the monitor's own or the row's rule K9, names --allow-source-change, which resolves it)
monitor.sources: the trainer hashes its sources once per session and gives the hash to this process, which refuses to run if its own differs (train2.sources)

absent.turn_q90_right: transitions/turn90_pi4_right: no reference within the thigh twist and the leg drives: the built reference is over a leg drive's Stage 0 limit
absent.turn_1_left: transitions/turn90_1_left: no reference within the thigh twist and the leg drives: the built reference is over a leg drive's Stage 0 limit; also outside heading_at_slowest_clock, post_window_zmp
absent.turn_1_right: transitions/turn90_1_right: no reference within the thigh twist and the leg drives: the built reference is over a leg drive's Stage 0 limit; also outside heading_at_slowest_clock
absent.inplace_left: transitions/start_inplace_0.5_left: the turn in place has no reference within the gates (inplace_0.5_left: Stage 0: over thigh twist use above 0.87 0.9114: blocks the freeze (thigh twist use above 0.87); start_inplace_0.5_left: Stage 0: over knee speed 1.1071; joint range margin under 0.05 rad (left_hip_yaw max) 0.0266: blocks the freeze (knee speed; joint range margin under 0.05 rad (left_hip_yaw max)))
absent.inplace_right: transitions/start_inplace_0.5_right: the turn in place has no reference within the gates (inplace_0.5_right: Stage 0: over thigh twist use above 0.87 0.9115: blocks the freeze (thigh twist use above 0.87); start_inplace_0.5_right: Stage 0: over knee speed 1.1664; joint range margin under 0.05 rad (right_hip_yaw min) 0.0266: blocks the freeze (knee speed; joint range margin under 0.05 rad (right_hip_yaw min)))

env.freeze_rule: rule K4: settings that name a freeze of the set (set_freeze: its manifest's sha256, the freeze the run started on) are accepted when, as the set is read today under its latest freeze, (1) every file this env's tasks use (and the nominal walk's) has the sha256 and the entry hash that the named freeze's manifest holds, and (2) the resolved task table is the same: a task is in the table under a freeze exactly when that freeze's manifest holds every file of its plan (a manifest lists every available entry), so with (1) the names, plans, window counts and lengths are the same; settings that name their tasks are read for those tasks alone.  Both are checked whether the named freeze is the set's latest or an earlier one (a set's records can be edited after its latest freeze without a new one).  Anything else is refused with what differs: a hash that is none of the set's freezes, a manifest that is not the one its hash names, a file missing from the named freeze, a changed file or entry, a task that entered or left the table (a named task that left it included).  Both freezes are in the env description, each with its index and manifest sha256: set_freeze_started is the named freeze, by the index of the first freeze of the set that holds that manifest (the settings hold the hash alone; sets.freeze appends no freeze whose manifest an earlier one holds), and never changes with a later freeze; set_freeze_now is the latest
env.crouch_rule: the track's LIPM frequency is control.omega0(p, q_home, crouch_frac = set.json's crouch_frac); no freeze covers set.json's own value and a freeze covers every walk entry's crouch_frac, so every walk entry whose file the library reads (the walks of every task the set holds, the nominal walk, the walks of a plan given as a plan) must record the same value: a set where they differ, or where such an entry records none, is refused with both values (as bar.set_crouch refuses it)
env.command_rule: the command (v, w) is piecewise constant on the reference clock, in the references' own units (the observation multiplies by the commanded clock rate): a hold (0, 0); a periodic walk or turn in place its entry's speed_m_s and yaw_rate_rad_s; a start, a change, a start into the turn in place and a stop the gait they lead to (gaits.b; a stand is (0, 0)) from the segment's first frame; a finite turn of angle A at rate w0 from walk a keeps a's speed and commands sign x |w0| for A / |w0| seconds of reference time from its first frame, then 0.  The commanded heading is the integral of w over reference time from the track's start; in a task whose definition names the heading "reference" (the turn-in-place tasks inplace_left and inplace_right, and no other) it is instead the reference's own yaw less its yaw at the track's start, at every reference time, with the command unchanged (a start into the turn commands its yaw rate from its first frame while the reference ramps up from rest; a walking turn keeps the integral).  Nothing before a segment's first frame depends on that segment; past the plan's end the last segment's command continues

core.layout_rule: actor (deployable): q, qd (the estimator's encoder angles and rates, plant joint order), gravity (-R[2] of the estimator's attitude), gyro, foot_load (over the nominal weight), phase (sin, cos of 2 pi the script's phase), support (the reference's flags), command ([v / 0.5 m/s, w / 1.0 rad/s] x the commanded clock rate), heading (the estimator's yaw about home less the commanded heading, over 0.5 rad, clipped to +-2; one input beyond plan B.1's list), prev_actions (the last three clipped, unfiltered actions, newest first), and on a body with a neck yaw and a jaw head_command ([yaw now, jaw now, yaw goal, jaw goal] / 0.6 rad).  Critic (privileged): root_vel (heading frame), height (over H), roll_pitch about home, dcm_error, joint_error (true less reference with the head overlay), heading_error (true yaw less the reference's), friction, floor (hard, robot_floor_carpet), push, plant_factors (mass, stiffness, delay / 24 ms, joint damping, joint friction), foot_error (the feet relative to the root in its heading frame, less the reference's), ref_contact (the reference's support 24 ms x the clock rate earlier).  Action: nj joint entries in plant order, then the clock
core.reward_rule: r = 0.55 joint + 0.35 tracking + 0.15 foot + 0.10 contact + 0.10 head - sum of the penalties x their weights; every term in [0, 1], read on the true state at the end of every env step (c the reference clock then, c0 at its start).  The true state: joint angles are those at the env step's end; body positions and orientations (the CoM, the trunk's attitude and yaw, the feet, the head, the feet's lowest points and slip speeds) and the foot loads are the plant's own after the env step's last physics step, which the simulator computes at that physics step's start, 2 ms before the env step's end (the plant's data is read, never recomputed).  What is read at every physics step (the foot loads, and with them a foot's contact, for contact, duty, flight, impact, touchdown, a foot's own lift-off and clearance (b); the foot bodies' heights for touchdown's speed; the actuator forces for servo) is likewise the plant's own after that physics step, computed at its start, and the reference's flags beside it are read at the reference clock after that physics step.  In an episode's first env step the displacement behind tracking's speed and yaw rate and behind progress's sample runs from the reading at the reset, which is of the episode's start, to the step's reading 18 ms later, and is divided by 20 ms like every other (it matters only for a start in motion).  A foot is loaded, or in contact, when its load is above 2 % of the true weight.  A kinematic playback of the reference scores joint, foot, contact and head 1, tracking close to 1 (a speed over the 20 ms step against the reference's at the step's start), progress below 1e-4 and every other penalty 0, except heading inside a finite walking turn, where the commanded heading is the integral of a rectangular yaw-rate pulse and the reference's own yaw ramps; duty, progress and clearance (a) are read so that it does.  joint: exp(-mean_j ((q_j - q_ref_j(c)) / 0.1 rad)^2) over all hinges, the reference with the head overlay.  tracking: Stage 1's gaussian_tracking_reward of the CoM's speed along the previous heading and the trunk's yaw rate over the step against the reference's own at c0 times the commanded clock rate.  foot: exp(-mean_f |r_f - r_ref_f(c)|^2 / (0.10 H)^2), r the foot body's position less the root's in the root's heading frame.  contact: the share, over both feet and the step's physics steps, of steps in which the foot's contact equals the reference's support at the clock or 24 ms x the clock rate earlier.  head: exp(-((roll - roll_ref)^2 + (pitch - pitch_ref)^2) / (3 deg)^2) of the head body in the world about home.  Penalties.  duty: min(1, sum over the feet read of max(0, lo - d_f, d_f - hi) / 0.05), d_f the foot's contact share over the physics steps of the last n env steps, n = round(the stride period at c / the clock rate / 20 ms), kept between 1 and 256 env steps (the history kept); a foot is read only where the reference's own support share for it over the same physics steps, each at the clock, lies inside the band [lo, hi], so that a start, a stop or a change, where the reference itself is outside the band, is not charged; the band is 0.55-0.72 while the commanded gait's target speed (the speed a rung's name holds, as the bar takes it; a gait whose name holds none: its entry's) is below 0.30 m/s, else 0.55-0.65; zero while the reference stands at c and until n env steps of the episode have been played.  slip: min(1, max(0, v - 0.05 m/s) / 0.05 m/s), v the largest horizontal speed of a foot, relative to what it touches, at its contacts that carry force, over the feet whose load is above 20 % of the true weight.  flight: the share of the env step's physics steps in which neither foot is loaded.  impact: min(1, max(0, F / the true weight - 1.6) / 1.6), F the largest sum of the two foot loads over the env step's physics steps.  tilt: min(1, max(0, max(|roll|, |pitch|) - 4 deg) / 4 deg) of the trunk about home.  clearance: the larger of (a) and (b).  (a): for a foot not in contact at the env step's end whose u = (c - c_lift) / T lies in [0.25, 0.75], min(1, max(0, 0.04 H - z) / (0.04 H)), z the height of the foot's lowest point above the floor; c_lift is the reference clock at the physics step in which the foot's own contact last ended (at an episode's start: for the foot the reference has in swing, the clock less the reference's swing progress x T; for the other foot, the clock) and T the planned length, in reference time, of the reference's swing in progress at c, in double support of its next swing and past its last swing of that one, each swing its own length, also inside a change of gait (a track that plans no complete swing: its gait's (1 - duty) x stride period); where T is not above zero, (a) is not read.  (b): 1 if in any physics step of the env step a foot is loaded while the reference has that foot between 25 % and 75 % of its swing both at the clock and 24 ms x the clock rate earlier.  action_rate: min(1, mean_i (a_i - a_prev_i)^2 / 0.25) on the clipped actions.  touchdown: in an env step in which a foot's contact begins, min(1, max(0, v_down - 0.15 m/s) / 0.30 m/s), v_down the foot body's downward speed one physics step before (the largest over the step's touchdowns).  servo: per drive that is no leg drive, a bias-corrected exponential mean of the squared actuator force (time constant 1.0 s), min(1, max(0, max_d RMS_d / sustained_d - 1) / 0.5).  interference: clip((3 mm - g) / 3 mm, 0, 1), g the smallest distance over the moving left-to-right leg pairs at the joint angles of the env step's end.  progress: zero unless c lies in a periodic walking segment (a gait whose commanded speed v_cmd is above zero) one stride period or more after the segment's first frame and the two means below have run one stride period of reference time; then min(1, max(0, (v_ref_bar - v_bar) / (rate x v_cmd)) / 0.10).  v_bar is the bias-corrected exponential mean (time constant: the stride period over the clock rate; one sample per env step; restarted at the segment's first frame, and started where an episode starts inside the segment) of the CoM's displacement over the env step along the commanded heading at c, over 20 ms.  v_ref_bar is the same mean over the same env steps of the reference's own sample: the clock rate x the reference CoM's progress along its own stride direction over the reference time the env step covered (in a segment's first step: from the segment's first frame), over that reference time.  The reference's mean over a stride is rate x v_cmd; its speed ripple inside a stride is in both means and charges nothing; a clock held slow leaves the reference's sample as it is and is charged in full.  heading: clip((|yaw - yaw_home - commanded heading(c)| - 3 deg) / 17 deg, 0, 1) on the true yaw, the difference wrapped to +-180 deg, zero in a hold; the commanded heading is the command rule's (in a turn-in-place task the reference's own yaw) and yaw_home is the true yaw at the episode's start less what the reference itself had turned by the start's reference time.  range: min(1, max_j max(0, required_j - margin_j) / 0.02 rad), margin the true joint's distance to its nearer limit (an end a joint rests on by design is none), required the script's.  progress, heading and range are beyond plan B.1's list (rule W5)
reward_readings: duty: a foot is charged only where the reference's own share over the same stride is inside the band
progress: the shortfall against the same mean of the reference's own speed, over rate x v_cmd
clearance (a): the planned length of the reference's swing in progress, on the reference clock

positions and foot loads: the plant's own after the env step's last physics step, computed at that physics step's start, and after every physics step for what is read there; joint angles: those at the env step's end
core.interference_rule: legs.LegGap at the end of every env step: the penalty reads the pairs that move (home distance at least the report cap); pairs that stay at one distance in every pose carry none and are listed; termination when the smallest distance over all pairs is below zero at two env-step ends in a row.  A one-pose contact is penalised, not terminated.  A leg against the trunk or the tail is not read

The true state: joint angles are those at the env step's end; body positions and orientations (the CoM, the trunk's attitude and yaw, the feet, the head, the feet's lowest points and slip speeds) and the foot loads are the plant's own after the env step's last physics step, which the simulator computes at that physics step's start, 2 ms before the env step's end (the plant's data is read, never recomputed).  What is read at every physics step (the foot loads, and with them a foot's contact, for contact, duty, flight, impact, touchdown, a foot's own lift-off and clearance (b); the foot bodies' heights for touchdown's speed; the actuator forces for servo) is likewise the plant's own after that physics step, computed at its start, and the reference's flags beside it are read at the reference clock after that physics step.  In an episode's first env step the displacement behind tracking's speed and yaw rate and behind progress's sample runs from the reading at the reset, which is of the episode's start, to the step's reading 18 ms later, and is divided by 20 ms like every other (it matters only for a start in motion).  A foot is loaded, or in contact, when its load is above 2 % of the true weight.  A kinematic playback of the reference scores joint, foot, contact and head 1, tracking close to 1 (a speed over the 20 ms step against the reference's at the step's start), progress below 1e-4 and every other penalty 0, except heading inside a finite walking turn, where the commanded heading is the integral of a rectangular yaw-rate pulse and the reference's own yaw ramps; duty, progress and clearance (a) are read so that it does.  joint: exp(-mean_j ((q_j - q_ref_j(c)) / 0.1 rad)^2) over all hinges, the reference with the head overlay.  tracking: Stage 1's gaussian_tracking_reward of the CoM's speed along the previous heading and the trunk's yaw rate over the step against the reference's own at c0 times the commanded clock rate.  foot: exp(-mean_f |r_f - r_ref_f(c)|^2 / (0.10 H)^2), r the foot body's position less the root's in the root's heading frame.  contact: the share, over both feet and the step's physics steps, of steps in which the foot's contact equals the reference's support at the clock or 24 ms x the clock rate earlier.  head: exp(-((roll - roll_ref)^2 + (pitch - pitch_ref)^2) / (3 deg)^2) of the head body in the world about home.  Penalties.  duty: min(1, sum over the feet read of max(0, lo - d_f, d_f - hi) / 0.05), d_f the foot's contact share over the physics steps of the last n env steps, n = round(the stride period at c / the clock rate / 20 ms), kept between 1 and 256 env steps (the history kept); a foot is read only where the reference's own support share for it over the same physics steps, each at the clock, lies inside the band [lo, hi], so that a start, a stop or a change, where the reference itself is outside the band, is not charged; the band is 0.55-0.72 while the commanded gait's target speed (the speed a rung's name holds, as the bar takes it; a gait whose name holds none: its entry's) is below 0.30 m/s, else 0.55-0.65; zero while the reference stands at c and until n env steps of the episode have been played.  slip: min(1, max(0, v - 0.05 m/s) / 0.05 m/s), v the largest horizontal speed of a foot, relative to what it touches, at its contacts that carry force, over the feet whose load is above 20 % of the true weight.  flight: the share of the env step's physics steps in which neither foot is loaded.  impact: min(1, max(0, F / the true weight - 1.6) / 1.6), F the largest sum of the two foot loads over the env step's physics steps.  tilt: min(1, max(0, max(|roll|, |pitch|) - 4 deg) / 4 deg) of the trunk about home.  clearance: the larger of (a) and (b).  (a): for a foot not in contact at the env step's end whose u = (c - c_lift) / T lies in [0.25, 0.75], min(1, max(0, 0.04 H - z) / (0.04 H)), z the height of the foot's lowest point above the floor; c_lift is the reference clock at the physics step in which the foot's own contact last ended (at an episode's start: for the foot the reference has in swing, the clock less the reference's swing progress x T; for the other foot, the clock) and T the planned length, in reference time, of the reference's swing in progress at c, in double support of its next swing and past its last swing of that one, each swing its own length, also inside a change of gait (a track that plans no complete swing: its gait's (1 - duty) x stride period); where T is not above zero, (a) is not read.  (b): 1 if in any physics step of the env step a foot is loaded while the reference has that foot between 25 % and 75 % of its swing both at the clock and 24 ms x the clock rate earlier.  action_rate: min(1, mean_i (a_i - a_prev_i)^2 / 0.25) on the clipped actions.  touchdown: in an env step in which a foot's contact begins, min(1, max(0, v_down - 0.15 m/s) / 0.30 m/s), v_down the foot body's downward speed one physics step before (the largest over the step's touchdowns).  servo: per drive that is no leg drive, a bias-corrected exponential mean of the squared actuator force (time constant 1.0 s), min(1, max(0, max_d RMS_d / sustained_d - 1) / 0.5).  interference: clip((3 mm - g) / 3 mm, 0, 1), g the smallest distance over the moving left-to-right leg pairs at the joint angles of the env step's end.  progress: zero unless c lies in a periodic walking segment (a gait whose commanded speed v_cmd is above zero) one stride period or more after the segment's first frame and the two means below have run one stride period of reference time; then min(1, max(0, (v_ref_bar - v_bar) / (rate x v_cmd)) / 0.10).  v_bar is the bias-corrected exponential mean (time constant: the stride period over the clock rate; one sample per env step; restarted at the segment's first frame, and started where an episode starts inside the segment) of the CoM's displacement over the env step along the commanded heading at c, over 20 ms.  v_ref_bar is the same mean over the same env steps of the reference's own sample: the clock rate x the reference CoM's progress along its own stride direction over the reference time the env step covered (in a segment's first step: from the segment's first frame), over that reference time.  The reference's mean over a stride is rate x v_cmd; its speed ripple inside a stride is in both means and charges nothing; a clock held slow leaves the reference's sample as it is and is charged in full.  heading: clip((|yaw - yaw_home - commanded heading(c)| - 3 deg) / 17 deg, 0, 1) on the true yaw, the difference wrapped to +-180 deg, zero in a hold; the commanded heading is the command rule's (in a turn-in-place task the reference's own yaw) and yaw_home is the true yaw at the episode's start less what the reference itself had turned by the start's reference time.  range: min(1, max_j max(0, required_j - margin_j) / 0.02 rad), margin the true joint's distance to its nearer limit (an end a joint rests on by design is none), required the script's.  progress, heading and range are beyond plan B.1's list (rule W5)
env.interference_rule: legs.LegGap at the end of every env step: the penalty reads the pairs that move (home distance at least the report cap); pairs that stay at one distance in every pose carry none and are listed; termination when the smallest distance over all pairs is below zero at two env-step ends in a row.  A one-pose contact is penalised, not terminated.  A leg against the trunk or the tail is not read
env.push_rule: with probability push_prob in an episode longer than 4 s: one push_s pulse at the trunk's CoM at a time uniform in [2 s, end - 2 s], direction uniform, dv = u x the body's Stage 0 forward bound (env.PUSH_BOUND_M_S[body]: no default), u uniform on push_walking if the reference walks at that time at the commanded clock and on push_standing if it stands; force = true mass x dv / push_s (rule J3)
env.factor_rule: per episode (rules J1, J2): servo delay k uniform on the integers latency_steps (inclusive), through speedfit.servo_delay; servo stiffness x kp; sliding friction; trunk mass and inertia x mass (env.MASS_RULE); joint damping and joint friction-loss, one factor each for all hinges; IMU noise scale.  The controller's model and feedforward stay nominal: every tracker is built on the nominal model before any episode
env.mid_start_rule: half of the episodes of every task but the stand start mid-task (rule T3): the reference time is uniform over the task's non-hold segments between 0.2 s after the first non-hold frame and 2.0 s x the clock rate before the plan's end, snapped to a file frame; the plant is set to that frame (rates x the clock rate) with Stage 1's start noise (uniform on the joints, uniform added to the root's velocity), the estimator is reset from that state, and the delay queue holds the k commands the zero action would have given before it.  The servos are then set to the oldest of those (without a delay, k = 0: to the command the zero action would have given one physics step before the start), the forward pass is computed once on that, and the estimator is reset again from the same state with a sensor reading of that pass (its foot loads, accelerometer and contact flags; the plant's first pass ran with the servos at their home targets)
env.reset_order: 1 the generator (a seeded reset restarts the episode stream); 2 the model's nominal arrays restored (friction, servo stiffness, joint damping and friction-loss, the masses and the constants MuJoCo derives from them); 3 the script (options.plan with options.seconds, else options.task, else a draw by the task weights) and its tracker, whose damping and friction-loss copies must be the nominal ones; 4 the start (options.start, else "mid" with probability mid_start where the script has mid spans, the reference time uniform on their union and snapped to a file frame); 5 the length; 6 the factors, drawn in the order friction, mass, kp, latency_steps, noise_scale, joint_damping, joint_friction, then options.factors, then applied; 7 the push and, on a body with a neck yaw and a jaw, the head script; 8 the episode seed and its start and noise seeds; 9 counters; 10 the previous episode's delay left; 11 the start; 12 the delay entered (a mid start refills its queue, sets the servos to the zero action's command before the start, computes the forward pass and gives the estimator its first reading from it); 13 the core's baselines, histories and accumulators, the observation
env.step_order: 1 the action clipped and low-passed; 2 R5: joint offsets and the clock factor on the tracker (None and exactly 1.0 for a zero action with the head neutral); R6: joint targets; 3 ten times: the push, the tracker's physics step, the step hook, the core's per-step readings; 4 the fall and any MuJoCo warning, the interference reading; 5 the counter, the reward; 6 terminated on a fall or on interference at two env-step ends in a row, truncated at the episode's length; 7 info and the observation
env.draw_order: from the env's own generator, in this order: the task; the start (one uniform for stance or mid, then the mid start's reference time); the factors (friction, mass, kp, latency_steps, noise_scale, joint_damping, joint_friction); the push (one uniform, then its time, its size and its direction); the head script (one uniform each for a gaze train and a jaw event, then their numbers).  The start's noise and the sensors' noise come from the episode seed (env.EPISODE_SEED_RULE), also at a mid start
env.mass_rule: the trunk's mass and inertia x the episode's factor, then every constant MuJoCo derives from the masses recomputed (mujoco.mj_setConst on a scratch MjData: the subtree masses behind subtree_com and every CoM reading, the constraint solver's invweight0 scales, dof_M0, actuator_acc0, the model's mean mass and inertia), so the plant is the model MuJoCo compiles with that trunk; every reset restores the nominal masses and constants the same way (mj_setConst leaves the nominal model unchanged bit for bit, checked when the env is built).  The controller keeps the nominal model (control.Tracker.model: the tracker's mass; R2's estimator, which computes the nominal model's CoM at its estimated pose; its sensors' noise scale): a deliberate model error, as a real robot's estimator has
env.episode_seed_rule: an episode given no seed is the env's k-th since its last seeded reset (k = 0, 1, ...): its seed is 1,000,000 x that reset's seed + k, so envs reset with different seeds never draw the same episode seed (train.SEED_RULE gives every run, session and env its own); the start's noise and the sensors' noise come from it (numpy SeedSequence([episode, 0]) and ([episode, 1])); the task, the plant factors and the push from the env's own generator
